summary: Latency regression: p95/p99 spikes tied to continuous-batching window (streaming requests experiencing timeouts)
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (Shoply) report intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional request timeouts for streaming generation routes since 2026-02-20 02:10 UTC. Spikes correlate with continuous-batching window increases on dedicated pool. Impact: customer-facing feature failures, elevated error rate (5xx) and streaming disconnects leading to degraded UX.

Impact:
- ~10% of streaming requests observe >2s additional latency; p99 up to 8-10s for some model routes.
- Intermittent 504/timeout responses observed when SDK client receives no bytes for >10s.
- Affects Shoply production dedicated pool (dedicated tier).

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: dedicated-pool-east-3
- Region: us-east
- Models: redwood-1-large (primary), redwood-1-quantized-8bit (fallback)
- Ingress via API gateway v2, customers using streaming endpoints (server-sent events / HTTP chunked)

Steps to reproduce:
1. Send steady stream of short-chat streaming requests (mean token length 30, QPS ~45) to Shoply's pinned route using redwood-1-large.
2. Observe p95/p99 latency in Console route dashboard.
3. Reproduce during off-peak and peak times; spikes appear independent of overall pool GPU utilization.

Expected behavior:
- p95/p99 should remain within historical baselines (p95 < 500ms for generation start; incremental token latency <50ms).

Observed behavior:
- p95 increases to 1.5-2s; p99 spikes to 8-10s in 10-20 minute windows.
- Streaming responses sometimes pause mid-stream for several seconds, then resume (indicating batching/aggregation delay).

Logs & metrics:
- Console: route latency and token latency graphs show step increases aligned to batching-window-duration metric bumps.
- Traces: sampled traces show requests waiting in serving-runtime for batch window to close (continuous-batching: wait_timer exceeded).
- Gateway logs: no upstream 5xxs, but downstream client disconnects recorded during pause intervals.
- No obvious GPU saturation or OOM; CPU and network metrics normal.
comments: 2026-02-20 03:05 - Support (Maya): Acknowledged issue and escalated to SRE. Requested logs and recent routing config from customer.
2026-02-20 04:12 - Customer (Shoply - Ben Carter): We're seeing live chat timeouts; funnel conversion dropped. We can provide request IDs and SDK logs on request.

2026-02-20 05:40 - SRE (Diego): Initial hypothesis: recent scheduler change to continuous-batching smoothing may be increasing batch window under certain QPS patterns. Gathering serving-runtime traces.

2026-02-20 08:25 - Eng (Nia Patel): Instrumented batch window and wait_timer metrics. Observed correlation between wait_timer events and p99 spikes. Opening PR to add debug logs when wait_timer triggers batch emission. (see related PRs)

2026-02-21 11:14 - Support (Maya): Provided customer with temporary workaround: pin route to 'redwood-1-large' non-quantized variant and set client-side streaming_keepalive to 5s. Customer will monitor.

2026-02-23 16:50 - SRE (Diego): Deployed a hotfix to serving-runtime to lower maximum continuous-batching window from 100ms to 50ms for dedicated pools as an emergency mitigation in us-east. Monitoring telemetry.
2026-02-24 09:30 - Customer (Ben Carter): After mitigation latency has returned to baseline for last 12 hours. No further timeouts observed.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Scheduler smoothing introduced an increased max wait timeout for continuous batching to improve throughput; under bursty short-request patterns this increases tail latency (observed).
Hypothesis 2: KV cache pressure causing backend to wait for larger batches when cold; low evidence (cache hit ratio normal).

Finding: Traces show requests sitting in serving-runtime queue waiting for batch window expiry (wait_timer trigger) rather than being dispatched immediately. This aligns with configured continuous-batching max_window_ms increasing to 100ms after recent scheduler tuning (commit 4f7b2a).
Related config change: scheduler PR #927 increased smoothing factor for batch window to prioritize throughput on longer sequences; unintended side-effect on high QPS short-seq workloads.
Mitigation verification: Hotfix reduced max continuous-batching window to 50ms -> p95 and p99 returned to baseline in affected routes. No measurable degradation in throughput for Shoply pool.

Follow-ups: add adaptive batching policy that considers request length distribution; add automated alerts when wait_timer percentile > configured threshold; run load tests for short-seq high-QPS pattern before future scheduler changes.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: hotfix deployed to serving-runtime in us-east (reduced max continuous-batching window to 50ms) and rollback of scheduler smoothing change for dedicated pools. Customer workaround: pinned to non-quantized model variant and applied client-side keepalive. Result: p95/p99 back to baseline; timeouts resolved.

Post-incident actions:
- Engineering: implement adaptive batching policy (task INT-338 to track).
- SRE: add alert for wait_timer p99 > 80ms on production pools.
- Product: update release checklist to include short-sequence high-QPS load tests for batching changes.

Status: Resolved for customer; internal follow-ups open. Customer confirmed recovery on 2026-02-24.
